title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter II of the 1986 notes 'Réalisations topologiques des réseaux' is about realizing combinatorial networks (graphs or ordered diagrams) by spaces. The basic building block is a 'ficelle' (string), F = (X, {A, B}). Here X is a space and A, B are two disjoint closed 'extremities'. A 'ligne' (line) C of F is a subspace that cuts X into two pieces, called 'feuilles' on the next page: X_{A,C}, containing A and bounded by C, and X_{B,C}, containing B and bounded by C. Each piece is again a ficelle: F_{A,C} = (X_{A,C}, {A, C}) and F_{B,C} = (X_{B,C}, {B, C}). Together they form the 'subdivided ficelles'.

Lemma (stated on this page, not proved). Let C be a line of F distinct from the extremities, and D a line of F_{B,C} distinct from its extremities. Then C is a line of F_{A,D} distinct from its extremities, and conversely. The figure shows a band with marks in the order A, C, D, B.

This is a transitivity, or 'associativity of cutting', statement. Cutting first at C and then at D gives the same three-piece decomposition as cutting first at D and then at C. Gluing pieces along lines is therefore associative. Consequently the lines of a ficelle, together with A and B, carry a betweenness relation, which with A < B gives a linear order: 'OPS A, B, C, D induits' and 'ordre des points'. The arrow line 'D,B,C ⇒ C,A,D ⇒ D,B,C' records the converse: the same lemma applied with the roles of A and B, and of C and D, exchanged.

The page continues the list of examples, from the previous page, of a topological property P imposed on extremities and lines. Example 1 (previous page): P = 'reduced to a point', which recovers topological ordered diagrams. Example 2 (this page): P = 'homeomorphic to B^n'. One then gets the theory of decompositions of a cylinder I×B^n ≃ B^{n+1}, with extremities {0}×B^n and {1}×B^n, by transverse 'lines' homeomorphic to B^n. The figures show this for n = 1: a rectangle, or a lens from A to B, cut by an arc C ≃ D^1 running from one long side to the other.

In modern terms, this is the composition of 'cylindrical' cobordisms or bordisms between n-balls: the one-dimensional, linearly ordered piece of a theory of topological realizations of networks. Each ficelle realizes an edge, and lines realize subdivision points.
errors: The lemma is stated without proof, and its truth depends on the precise definition of 'ligne' (which is on earlier pages). One needs C to lie in the interior of X_{A,D}, and the two pieces of a cut to meet exactly in the line.

In example 2, merely asking that lines be homeomorphic to B^n is insufficient for n ≥ 2. A wildly embedded ball (Alexander horned sphere phenomena) can separate I×B^n so that the pieces are not balls or cylinders. Some local flatness or collar condition is needed. Grothendieck adds such a condition on the next page: a neighbourhood of C of the form C×]-1,1[ whose two 'rives' lie in the two feuilles. He also mentions tubular-neighbourhood boundaries on the previous page.

ideas.what: Ficelle (string) = space with two extremities; lines cutting it into two sub-ficelles; the lemma that cutting is associative/transitive, giving a linear order on lines
ideas.modern_name: Composition of bordisms/cobordisms; linear (betweenness) order of separating subsets; one-dimensional piece of a stratified realization of a graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore of cobordism composition (Milnor, Thom); betweenness/order from separation goes back to classical continuum theory (Moore, Kline, Ward)

ideas.what: Example: lines homeomorphic to B^n in the cylinder I×B^n ≃ B^{n+1}, giving decompositions of a ball into stacked ball-slabs
ideas.modern_name: Decompositions of a cylinder by properly embedded locally flat balls (h-cobordism/collar-type slicing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL/topological manifold theory (Brown's collaring theorem, Schoenflies-type results)

deep.surprise_reason: A foundational, routine lemma (associativity of cutting a bordism-like 'string') and a standard example. It is part of an unpublished but elementary setup for realizing networks topologically, with no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The right-hand column after 'Être homéomorphe à B^n :' reads roughly 'On trouve notamment la théorie des décompositions'; the word read as 'seulement' is more likely 'notamment', and the '[?] décomposition' is possibly 'bi-décomposition', cf. '2 décomposition' on the next page.
'OPS A, B, C, D induits : ... des points' — likely 'ordre des points'; the crossed-out phrase is 'Ficelle orientée'.
The leading 'ou' in the left margin belongs before 'de I×B ≃ B^{n+1}', i.e. '... ou de I×B^n ≃ B^{n+1}'.
The 'T' / '⊤' before 'D, B, C' is probably a stray mark or an 'I', not a logical symbol.
